facts.statement: The genus Lotosaurus was named by Fa-kui Zhang in 1975, with Lotosaurus adentus as the type species.
facts.quote: Lotosaurus was first named by Fa-kui Zhang in 1975 and the type species is Lotosaurus adentus.

facts.statement: The holotype of Lotosaurus is the well-preserved, articulated skeleton IVPP V 4881 (or possibly V 4880).
facts.quote: Lotosaurus is known from the holotype IVPP V 4881 (or possibly V 4880), an articulated and well-preserved skeleton.

facts.statement: At least 38 individuals of Lotosaurus died in a single location, representing various ages.
facts.quote: At least 38 individuals of various ages died within this one location.

facts.statement: Lotosaurus fossils have been found in Hunan Province in central China.
facts.quote: Lotosaurus is an extinct genus of sail-backed poposauroid known from Hunan Province of central China.

facts.statement: Lotosaurus was a heavily built quadruped measuring between 1.5 and 2.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Lotosaurus was 1.5 to 2.5 m long and a heavily built quadruped.

facts.statement: Lotosaurus was a herbivore that used its toothless, beaked jaws to shear off leaves.
facts.quote: It was a herbivore, shearing off leaves with its toothless, beaked jaws.

facts.statement: Lotosaurus possessed a sail on its back, giving it an appearance similar to Permian pelycosaurs like Dimetrodon, though the sail was not as high.
facts.quote: Lotosaurus, like some other members of the Poposauroidea, had a sail on its back, granting it an appearance superficially similar to that of Permian pelycosaurs like Dimetrodon and Edaphosaurus, although not as high.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic analyses by Sterling J. Nesbitt in 2011 classified Lotosaurus as a member of the group Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: Sterling J. Nesbitt (2011) found Lotosaurus to be a member of the group Poposauroidea.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Lotosaurus lived in a subtropical environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: The mineral and microfossil composition of the site suggests that it was a subtropical environment, with pronounced wet and dry seasons.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Lotosaurus may have died from thirst or sickness during the dry season while gathered around a watering hole.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that the group perished due to thirst or sickness during the dry season, perhaps while gathered around an evaporating or contaminated watering hole.

facts.statement: A 2019 study determined the maximum depositional age of the Lotosaurus fossils to be 238.0 ± 1.4 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.
facts.quote: A subsequent 2019 study weighted mean age of 238.0 ± 1.4 Ma (Ladinian) as the maximum depositional age for the sandstones preserving fossils of Lotosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Lotosaurus was endemic to the South China Craton or immigrated from the North China Craton, with immigration currently considered more likely due to the presence of relatives elsewhere.
facts.quote: Considering that close relatives of Lotosaurus (the shuvosaurids) lived in other regions of Pangaea around that time, the latter hypothesis is currently believed to be more likely.

rejected.statement: Poposauroidea, the group containing Lotosaurus, is part of the reptile lineage Pseudosuchia, which also includes aetosaurs, raisuchids, and modern crocodilians.
rejected.quote: Poposauroids were part of Pseudosuchia, the lineage of reptiles which also includes aetosaurs, raisuchids, and modern crocodilians.
